ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A square coil with an area of S＝4×10－2 m2 and a number of turns n＝100 is placed in a uniform magnetic field. The direction of the magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane of the coil. The law by which the magnetic induction intensity B changes with time t is as shown in Figure 9. At the instant t＝0, the direction of the magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane of the coil and inward. Then which of the following judgments is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: During 1～2 s, the direction of the current in the coil is clockwise

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in Figure 9, a square coil with an area of S=4×10-2 m2 and a number of turns n=100 is placed in a uniform magnetic field. The direction of the magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane of the coil, and the magnetic induction intensity B changes with time t. It is known that at the instant t=0, the direction of the magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane of the coil and inward. Question: during 1~2 s, what is the direction of the induced current in the coil?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: During 1~2 s, the direction of the current in the coil is clockwise
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the graph: in the figure, the vertical axis is B/T, and the horizontal axis is t/s. The curve shows that at t=0, B=+2 T; from t=0 to 2 s, B decreases linearly, is 0 at t=1 s, and is -2 T at t=2 s; afterward, from t=2 to 4 s, it again increases linearly to +2 T. Therefore, during 1~2 s, B changes from 0 to -2 T. Then reason: the problem gives that at t=0, the magnetic field direction is perpendicular to the plane of the coil and inward, while in the figure t=0 corresponds to B being a positive value, so the positive direction represents the magnetic field being inward. During 1~2 s, B is negative and its absolute value increases, indicating that the outward magnetic flux is increasing. According to Lenz's law, the magnetic field produced by the induced current must hinder this change, so it should produce an inward magnetic field. By the right-hand rule, the current direction corresponding to producing an inward magnetic field in the coil is clockwise.
